caseTitle.en: The blister under the moxa tube

condition.zh: 安全 · 艾灸燙傷處理

title.en: Night shift on the integrative ward

tagline.zh: 一位感覺不到熱的阿伯、一個不痛的水泡，和一通說實話的電話
tagline.en: A man who cannot feel heat, a blister that does not hurt, and a phone call that tells the truth

desc.zh: 今晚整合病房的中醫值班。看傷口、寫紀錄、打那通最難打的電話。
desc.en: Tonight’s TCM on-call on the integrative ward. Assess the wound, write it up, and make the hardest phone call.

desc.zh: 巡房、翻身、換藥、測血糖。今晚第一個發現水泡的人是你。
desc.en: Rounds, turns, dressings, glucose checks. Tonight you are the one who finds the blister.

about.zh: 二十年前親手燙傷過一位病人。從此每一個灸盒，他都先用自己的手背試溫。這件事他會親口告訴你。
about.en: Burned a patient himself twenty years ago. Ever since, he tests every moxa box on the back of his own hand. He will tell you about it himself.

about.zh: 夜班第五年。看水泡的眼光比皮膚科還挑，量血糖比誰都快。
about.en: Fifth year of nights. Judges a blister more strictly than dermatology and checks a glucose faster than anyone.

role.zh: 七十二歲，中風後復健、糖尿病

about.zh: 虛構教學個案。左側中風後在整合病房復健，糖尿病多年，兩腳麻。說話慢，笑話多。今晚心情不好，晚餐沒吃完。
about.en: Fictional teaching case. Rehabilitating after a left-sided stroke on the integrative ward; diabetic for years, both feet numb. Slow speech, plenty of jokes. In a mood tonight; left half his dinner.

about.zh: 每天下班來陪爸爸。看網路影片買了一個溫灸筒，想讓爸爸的腳暖一點。
about.en: Visits her father after work every day. Bought a moxa warming tube after watching videos online, to warm his feet.

about.zh: 照會回覆永遠附三句：拍照、別刺破、別塗偏方。
about.en: Every consult reply ends with three lines: photograph it, don’t pop it, no home remedies.

plain.zh: 糖尿病傷到末梢神經，腳麻、對冷熱痛不敏感。感覺不到燙，就容易被燙傷。
plain.en: Diabetes damaging the nerve endings: numb feet, poor sense of hot, cold and pain. If you cannot feel heat, you get burned.

plain.zh: 內放點燃艾條、用綁帶固定在穴位上的金屬筒；方便，但綁久了熱會累積。
plain.en: A metal tube holding a lit moxa stick, strapped over a point; convenient, but heat builds up the longer it stays.

plain.zh: 放在腹部或背部的木盒，艾條在盒內燃燒；施灸全程要有人看。
plain.en: A wooden box on the belly or back with moxa burning inside; someone watches the whole time.

plain.zh: 施灸者把手指放在穴位兩旁感受溫度，替感覺遲鈍的病人把關。
plain.en: The operator rests fingers beside the point to feel the heat on behalf of a patient who cannot.

plain.zh: 一度只紅；淺二度有水泡、很痛；深二度發白斑駁、較不痛；三度像皮革、不痛。
plain.en: First degree is red only; superficial partial-thickness blisters and hurts; deep partial-thickness is pale and blotchy, less painful; full-thickness is leathery and painless.

plain.zh: 燙傷後盡早用流動的冷水（不是冰水）沖，持續一段時間，降低組織溫度。
plain.en: Cool, not iced, running water on a burn as soon as possible and for a good while, to draw heat out of the tissue.

plain.zh: 不會黏在傷口上的無菌敷料，換藥時不會把新皮撕掉。
plain.en: A sterile dressing that does not stick to the wound, so changing it does not tear new skin.

plain.zh: 古代刻意在穴位燒出灸瘡、留下疤痕的直接灸；現代少用，須充分說明與同意。
plain.en: An old direct method that deliberately raises a moxa sore and leaves a scar; rare today and only with full explanation and consent.

plain.zh: 中風後常見證型：氣不足推不動血，肢體無力、舌淡紫。
plain.en: A common pattern after stroke: too little qi to move the blood, weak limbs, a pale-purple tongue.

plain.zh: 伸舌偏向一側，中風常見。舊的舌歪是後遺症，新出現的舌歪是急症。
plain.en: The tongue points to one side when stuck out, common after stroke. An old deviation is a sequel; a new one is an emergency.

plain.zh: 醫療過程中發生傷害或差點發生時填寫的報告，目的是改進系統，不是找人處罰。
plain.en: The report filed when harm happens, or nearly happens, during care; its purpose is to fix the system, not to punish someone.

plain.zh: 不良事件後，誠實告訴病人與家屬發生什麼、怎麼處理、如何避免再發生。
plain.en: After an adverse event, telling the patient and family honestly what happened, what is being done, and how it will be prevented.

plain.zh: 冒冷汗、手抖、心悸、反應變慢；糖尿病人晚餐吃少的夜裡最常見。
plain.en: Cold sweat, tremor, racing heart, slowed responses; commonest at night in a diabetic who ate little at dinner.

text.zh: 金屬筒內插艾條，用綁帶固定在穴位上。綁帶一鬆，筒底就直接貼住皮膚。病房裡還有氧氣：明火要在醫護手上，不在家屬手上。
text.en: A metal tube holding a moxa stick, strapped over a point. If the strap slips, the hot base rests on the skin. And wards have oxygen: open flame stays with staff, never with visitors.

text.zh: 腹部大面積溫灸用。何醫師的規矩：放上去之前先用手背試溫，綁好，蓋子留縫，旁邊有人，感覺遲鈍的地方不放。
text.en: For warming a wide belly area. Dr Ho’s rules: test it on the back of your hand first, strap it, leave the lid ajar, stay beside it, and never on numb skin.

name.zh: 何醫師的「手指感溫」小卡

text.zh: 一張護貝小卡：「你的手指，是他的皮膚。」背面寫著二十年前那位病人的名字縮寫，和一句「對不起」。
text.en: A laminated card: “Your fingers are his skin.” On the back, the initials of a patient from twenty years ago, and the words “I’m sorry.”

text.zh: 一、停止施灸、移開熱源。二、盡早以流動冷水沖一段時間；不用冰、不塗牙膏醬油或偏方。三、輕輕移除周圍衣物飾品，黏住的不撕。四、評估範圍與深度；不痛不代表淺，神經病變的人尤其如此。五、小水泡保持完整，以無菌非黏性敷料覆蓋；大水泡、深二度以上、臉手腳會陰或糖尿病足：照會傷口照護或整形外科。六、記錄、拍照、通報、據實告知。注意破傷風疫苗狀態。
text.en: One: stop the moxa, remove the heat. Two: cool running water early and for a good while; no ice, toothpaste, soy sauce or folk remedies. Three: gently remove clothing and jewellery nearby; leave anything stuck. Four: assess area and depth; no pain does not mean shallow, especially with neuropathy. Five: keep small blisters intact under a sterile non-adherent dressing; large blisters, deep or worse burns, face, hands, feet, perineum or a diabetic foot go to wound care or plastic surgery. Six: record, photograph, report, disclose. Check tetanus status.

name.en: Moxa for people who cannot feel heat

text.zh: 糖尿病神經病變、中風患側、脊髓損傷、意識不清、失智與幼兒，都無法可靠地說「燙」。中醫的溫補思路仍可用，但要換地方、換方法：選感覺正常的部位，用施灸者的手指感溫，縮短而頻繁地檢查皮膚，不用綁住不管的器具，不讓家屬自行施灸。
text.en: Diabetic neuropathy, the affected side after stroke, spinal injury, reduced consciousness, dementia and small children cannot reliably say “too hot”. The warming idea of TCM can still apply, but change the site and the method: choose skin with normal sensation, let the operator’s fingers feel the heat, check the skin briefly and often, avoid strapped-on devices left unwatched, and never let visitors do it themselves.

name.zh: 不良事件：通報與據實告知

text.zh: 發生傷害後，先處理病人，再說實話：發生了什麼、我們做了什麼、接下來怎麼做、怎麼避免再發生。不猜測、不推責、不隱瞞，也不急著認定是誰的錯。異常事件通報是為了找出系統的漏洞，例如：家屬不知道病房不能自行施灸、交班沒寫清楚哪一側不灸。
text.en: After harm, treat the patient first, then tell the truth: what happened, what we did, what comes next, how it will be prevented. No guessing, no blame-shifting, no hiding, and no rush to decide whose fault it was. Incident reports exist to find the gaps in the system: a family who did not know moxa is not self-administered on the ward, a handover that did not say which side must not be warmed.

text.zh: 古籍有「灸瘡」之說，認為灸後發瘡化膿能增強療效，因此有刻意的瘢痕灸。它是有計畫、經同意、在選定穴位上的治療，現代已很少使用。意外燙傷則是沒有計畫、沒有同意、常在感覺遲鈍處發生的傷害。兩者不能混為一談，更不能拿古籍替意外解釋。
text.en: Classical texts speak of the moxa sore, holding that a sore that festers strengthens the effect, hence deliberate scarring moxibustion. That is planned, consented, on chosen points, and rare today. An accidental burn is unplanned, unconsented and usually on numb skin. The two must never be confused, and the classics must never be used to explain away an accident.

note.en: Uncle Kuo: no moxa on the left

lines.zh: 交班。郭阿伯，七十二歲，左側中風後復健，糖尿病，兩腳麻。
lines.en: Handover. Uncle Kuo, seventy-two, rehab after a left-sided stroke, diabetic, both feet numb.

lines.zh: 下午開始溫灸：關元、氣海用灸盒，皮膚正常。交班寫「左下肢感覺遲鈍，不灸」。
lines.en: Moxa started this afternoon: box on Guanyuan and Qihai, skin fine. Handover note says “left leg numb, no moxa”.

lines.zh: 在掛圖上指給我看白天的灸位，再告訴我，哪個穴今晚不能碰。
lines.en: Show me today’s moxa points on the chart, then tell me which one is off-limits tonight.

q.en: Point to Guanyuan, Qihai and Zusanli

post.zh: 足三里本來也在處方上，但左腳麻，所以拿掉了。
post.en: Zusanli was on the plan too, but the left leg is numb, so it came off.

post.zh: 選穴沒錯。中醫認為中風後氣虛血瘀，溫灸關元氣海補氣。錯，常常錯在「哪一隻腳」。
post.en: The points were sound. In TCM post-stroke qi deficiency with blood stasis is warmed at Guanyuan and Qihai. Mistakes usually come down to “which leg”.

note.zh: 舌歪是舊的，腳冰是真的

lines.zh: 醫師，晚餐太難吃，我吃一半。你們中醫可以開好吃的藥嗎？
lines.en: Doctor, dinner was awful; I ate half. Can Chinese medicine prescribe something tasty?

lines.zh: 先讓我看看舌頭。
lines.en: Let me look at your tongue first.

lines.zh: 我的舌頭伸得比我左手還直。
lines.en: My tongue sticks out straighter than my left arm.

q.zh: 舌淡紫、苔薄白，伸舌偏向一側。中風後三個月。辨證？
q.en: Pale-purple, thin white coat, pointing to one side. Three months after the stroke. The pattern?

options.zh: 氣虛血瘀，舌歪為中風舊象

why.zh: 舌淡為氣虛，紫為血瘀；舌歪是中風留下的。中醫認為治在補氣活血。若舌歪是新出現的，就是急症。
why.en: Pale means qi deficiency, purple means stasis; the deviation is left over from the stroke. TCM treats by tonifying qi and moving blood. A deviation that is new would be an emergency.

options.zh: 肝陽上亢，馬上會再中風
options.en: Liver yang rising; another stroke now

why.zh: 肝陽上亢舌紅苔黃、脈弦有力。他的舌是淡紫，舌歪也是舊的。
why.en: Liver yang shows a red tongue, yellow coat and forceful wiry pulse. His is pale-purple and the deviation is old.

why.zh: 陰虛舌紅少苔。他的舌淡、苔薄白。
why.en: Yin deficiency gives a red tongue with scant coat. His is pale with a thin white coat.

why.zh: 痰熱腑實苔黃膩、便秘、口臭。都沒有。
why.en: Phlegm-heat with constipation brings a greasy yellow coat, constipation, bad breath. None here.

post.zh: 舊的舌歪不用緊張。新的舌歪、新的說話不清，立刻叫中風小組。
post.en: An old deviated tongue is no cause for alarm. A new one, or new slurred speech, means calling the stroke team at once.

lines.zh: 爸的腳好冰。我看影片說灸足三里會暖，晚上可以幫他嗎？
lines.en: Dad’s feet are icy. A video said moxa on Zusanli warms you up. Can I do it for him tonight?

lines.zh: 左腳他感覺不到燙，病房也有氧氣。先穿襪子、蓋毯子，灸的事明天醫師決定。
lines.en: He can’t feel heat in the left leg, and there’s oxygen on the ward. Socks and a blanket for now; moxa is the doctor’s call tomorrow.

lines.zh: 好……我只是想讓他舒服一點。
lines.en: OK... I only wanted him to be comfortable.

lines.zh: 左小腿外側綁著一個溫灸筒，綁帶鬆了，筒底貼著皮膚。郭小姐的包包已經不在椅子上。
lines.en: A warming tube is strapped to the outside of his left shin. The strap has slipped and the hot base sits on the skin. Ms Kuo’s bag is gone from the chair.

lines.zh: 我移開了。下面一個硬幣大的水泡，周圍一圈紅。
lines.en: I’ve taken it off. Underneath, a blister the size of a coin with a red ring around it.

lines.zh: 不痛啊。你們幹嘛這麼緊張？
lines.en: Doesn’t hurt. Why all the fuss?

lines.zh: 因為他不會痛，所以我們要緊張。第一步？
lines.en: Because he can’t feel it, we have to. First step?

q.zh: 灸後水泡，熱源已移開。下一步？
q.en: A moxa blister, heat source removed. Next?

options.en: Cool running water, for a good while

why.zh: 盡早用流動冷水降溫，能減少熱繼續往深處傷害。不用冰，糖尿病人的循環更經不起。
why.en: Cool running water early stops heat from burning deeper. No ice; a diabetic’s circulation can least afford it.

why.zh: 冰會讓血管收縮，加深組織損傷，還可能凍傷。
why.en: Ice narrows the vessels, deepens the injury and can cause frostbite.

why.zh: 偏方會刺激傷口、增加感染，還遮住判讀。
why.en: Home remedies irritate the wound, invite infection and hide what you need to see.

why.zh: 完整的水泡是天然敷料。刺破就多一個感染入口。
why.en: An intact blister is a natural dressing. Popping it opens a door for infection.

post.zh: 處置室的洗手台，我推輪椅帶他過去沖。
post.en: The treatment-room sink. I’ll wheel him over and rinse it there.

lines.zh: 等一下。不冰、不塗、不刺破。冰會讓血管收縮，偏方會感染。我們沖流動冷水。
lines.en: Hold on. No ice, no remedies, no popping. Ice narrows the vessels; remedies infect. We use cool running water.

lines.zh: 沖完了，看傷口。不痛，就是淺的嗎？
lines.en: Cooled. Now look at it. No pain means shallow?

lines.zh: 不一定。他有周邊神經病變，痛不能拿來判斷深度。
lines.en: Not necessarily. He has peripheral neuropathy; pain can’t be used to judge depth.

question.zh: 灸後水泡、病人不痛。怎麼判斷燙傷深度？
question.en: A moxa blister in a man who feels no pain. How do you judge burn depth?

answer.zh: 看外觀不看痛：完整水泡、底部粉紅濕潤、壓了會變白再回紅，多為淺二度；底部發白斑駁、回紅慢，可能是深二度；像皮革、乾硬則是三度。神經病變的人疼痛不可靠，糖尿病足部與深二度以上要照會傷口照護。
answer.en: Look, don’t ask about pain: an intact blister on a pink, moist base that blanches and refills is usually superficial partial-thickness; a pale, blotchy base that refills slowly may be deep partial-thickness; leathery and dry is full-thickness. In neuropathy pain is unreliable; diabetic feet and anything deeper go to wound care.

post.zh: 底部粉紅、會回紅，水泡完整。我拍照、記範圍。
post.en: Pink base, refills, blister intact. I’ll photograph it and record the size.

post.zh: 大概是淺二度。但糖尿病的腿，好得慢、容易感染。照會傷口照護。
post.en: Probably superficial partial-thickness. But a diabetic leg heals slowly and infects easily. Consult wound care.

lines.zh: 你排給我看，我們今晚做的每一步。
lines.en: Put tonight’s steps in order for me.

q.en: Managing a moxa burn, in order

steps.en: Stop the moxa, remove the heat
Cool running water for a good while
Ease clothing off; leave anything stuck

steps.zh: 看外觀評估範圍與深度
steps.en: Judge area and depth by appearance

steps.zh: 水泡保持完整，覆蓋非黏性敷料
steps.en: Keep the blister intact; non-adherent dressing

post.zh: 非黏性敷料貼好了。明天換藥不會撕掉新皮。
post.en: Non-adherent dressing on. Tomorrow’s change won’t tear the new skin.

guide.en: Listen to Dr Ho at the station

lines.zh: 二十年前，我把灸盒放在一位中風阿嬤的肚子上，去接了一通電話。
lines.en: Twenty years ago I put a moxa box on a stroke patient’s belly and went to take a phone call.

lines.zh: 回來的時候，她肚子上有一個水泡。她也說不痛。
lines.en: When I came back she had a blister on her belly. She said it didn’t hurt either.

lines.zh: 後來呢？
lines.en: What happened?

lines.zh: 我告訴她女兒是我的錯。從那天起，每一個灸盒我都先放在自己手背上。
lines.en: I told her daughter it was my fault. Since that day every moxa box goes on the back of my hand first.

post.zh: 溫灸筒、灸盒，都不是「綁上去就好」的東西。距離、時間、有人看，三樣都要。
post.en: Tubes and boxes are never “strap it on and walk away”. Distance, time, and someone watching: all three.

guide.en: Practise securing a moxa box safely

lines.zh: 明天白天如果還要灸關元，你來放。先手背試溫，再固定，再用手指感溫。
lines.en: If Guanyuan gets moxa tomorrow, you place it. Back-of-hand test, then secure it, then the finger heat-check.

guide.en: Ask Dr Ho about scarring moxa

lines.zh: 古書不是說灸瘡發了才有效嗎？阿伯這個算不算？
lines.en: Don’t the old books say moxa only works once a sore forms? Does his count?

lines.zh: 瘢痕灸是有計畫、經同意、在選好的穴位上做。今晚這個，是意外。
lines.en: Scarring moxibustion is planned, consented and on chosen points. Tonight was an accident.

post.zh: 不要拿古籍替意外找理由。病人家屬第一個會問的，就是這個。
post.en: Never use the classics to explain away an accident. It’s the first thing families ask.

lines.zh: 我爸睡了嗎？我剛剛幫他灸了腳，他說很舒服，我就先回家了。
lines.en: Is Dad asleep? I did moxa on his leg earlier; he said it felt nice, so I went home.

lines.zh: 這通電話是你的。我在旁邊。
lines.en: This call is yours. I’m right here.

q.zh: 郭小姐不知道發生了什麼。你怎麼說？
q.en: Ms Kuo doesn’t know what happened. What do you say?

options.zh: 說明事實、處置與後續，不責怪
options.en: Facts, care given, next steps; no blame

why.zh: 據實告知：發生什麼、做了什麼、接下來怎麼做。她出於好意，也是我們沒把病房規則講清楚。
why.en: Open disclosure: what happened, what was done, what happens next. She acted out of love, and we had not made the ward rules clear.

options.zh: 說是皮膚過敏，明天再說
options.en: Call it a skin allergy; explain tomorrow

why.zh: 隱瞞會讓信任崩掉，她明天看到敷料一定會問。
why.en: Hiding it destroys trust, and she will ask the moment she sees the dressing.

options.en: Tell her it was her fault

why.zh: 責怪不會讓傷口好，也不會讓下一個家屬學到。系統也有漏洞。
why.en: Blame heals nothing and teaches the next family nothing. The system had gaps too.

post.en: ...It was me. I thought I was helping.

post.zh: 妳是在幫他。是我們沒先講清楚：他的左腳感覺不到燙，病房不能自己點火。
post.en: You were trying to. We hadn’t made it clear: his left leg can’t feel heat, and no one lights a flame on the ward.

lines.zh: 「皮膚過敏」這四個字，明早她看到敷料就會拆穿。現在打回去，從頭說一次。
lines.en: Those words “skin allergy” fall apart when she sees the dressing tomorrow. Call her back now and start again.

guide.zh: 寫紀錄與異常事件通報
guide.en: Write the notes and the incident report

lines.zh: 通報：家屬自行使用溫灸筒於感覺遲鈍之左小腿，綁帶鬆脫致淺二度燙傷。
lines.en: Report: family applied a moxa tube to the numb left shin; strap slipped; superficial partial-thickness burn.

lines.zh: 改善建議：入院衛教寫明病房禁止自行施灸；交班註明不灸側並掛床頭。
lines.en: Suggestions: admission teaching states no self-administered moxa; handover marks the no-moxa side, with a sign at the bedside.

lines.zh: 通報不是寫誰的錯，是寫哪個洞要補。你寫對了。
lines.en: An incident report isn’t about whose fault; it’s about which hole to fill. You got it right.

guide.en: Chia-Jung says Uncle Kuo seems off

lines.zh: 巡房時，阿伯滿頭冷汗，手在抖。叫他名字，他慢了好幾拍才回答。
lines.en: On her round, Uncle Kuo is drenched in cold sweat, his hands shaking. When she says his name, he answers several beats late.

lines.zh: 是燙傷在痛嗎？可是他腳麻啊。
lines.en: Is the burn hurting? But his legs are numb.

options.zh: 測指尖血糖，依流程處理並通知醫師
options.en: Fingerstick glucose, protocol, call the doctor

why.zh: 糖尿病人夜裡冒冷汗、手抖、反應慢，先想低血糖。他晚餐只吃一半。測血糖、依低血糖流程處理、通知醫師再追蹤。
why.en: Night sweats, tremor and slowed responses in a diabetic: think low sugar first. He ate half his dinner. Check the glucose, follow the hypoglycaemia protocol, call the doctor, recheck.

why.zh: 先找原因。低血糖不處理，針再多也醒不過來。
why.en: Find the cause first. Untreated low sugar won’t respond to any needle.

options.zh: 給止痛藥，以為是燙傷痛

why.zh: 他對痛不敏感。冷汗加反應慢，不是傷口痛的樣子。
why.en: He barely feels pain. Sweat and slowness are not what wound pain looks like.

options.en: Let him sleep; review in the morning

why.zh: 夜間低血糖拖到早上可能抽搐或昏迷。
why.en: Overnight hypoglycaemia left till morning can end in seizures or coma.

post.zh: 血糖很低。依流程處理了，他醒過來第一句是：「我晚餐沒吃完。」
post.en: Very low. Treated per protocol. The first thing he said when he came round: “I didn’t finish my dinner.”

post.zh: 冷汗不一定是痛。糖尿病人夜裡冒汗，先想血糖。
post.en: Sweat isn’t always pain. A diabetic sweating at night: think sugar first.

post.zh: 早知道就把那難吃的晚餐吃完。
post.en: Should have finished that awful dinner.

lines.zh: 血糖追蹤我依流程排好了，傷口敷料也看過，乾的。
lines.en: I’ve scheduled glucose rechecks per protocol, and checked the dressing: dry.

lines.zh: 溫灸筒我收進護理站，貼上「家屬請勿自行使用」。
lines.en: The moxa tube is locked in the station, labelled “Not for family use”.

sub.zh: 照會已收到，明早第一個看

lines.zh: 已收到照會，明早第一個看郭阿伯。請拍照記錄、勿刺破、勿塗偏方。
lines.en: Consult received; Uncle Kuo is first on my list tomorrow. Please photograph it, don’t pop it, no home remedies.

lines.zh: 郭小姐傳訊息來：「謝謝你們告訴我。明天我帶早餐給爸，陪他吃完。」
lines.en: Message from Ms Kuo: “Thank you for telling me. I’ll bring Dad breakfast tomorrow and make sure he finishes it.”

lines.zh: 今晚一個水泡、一次低血糖、一通電話。哪一個最難？
lines.en: Tonight: one blister, one low sugar, one phone call. Which was hardest?

lines.zh: 電話。
lines.en: The call.

lines.zh: 對。傷口兩週會好，信任要更久。這張卡給你，背面那個名字，是我的那一位。
lines.en: Yes. The wound heals in a couple of weeks; trust takes longer. Have this card. The name on the back is my patient.

lines.zh: 卡片正面寫著：「你的手指，是他的皮膚。」
lines.en: The front reads: “Your fingers are his skin.”

sub.en: Stop, cool, look, cover, tell the truth
